long.title: The reading group picked a book about gardens, belonging and the rooms we leave behind
long.body: Our group chose a novel with three narrators, and we are making room for readers who want to join halfway through. We will discuss the first section on Sunday, then spend the next week comparing the garden scenes with the kitchen scenes. If you have a passage that changed how you understood the family, bring it along. There is no need to finish the book before joining the conversation.

one.author: Hana Sato
one.text: What was your final proof time? Mine always collapse past 14 hours.

long.author: Matteo Bianchi of the Riverside Bread and Community Oven Workshop
long.text: I let the flour and water sit for ninety minutes before adding the starter. That made the dough easier to fold, but the flavor mostly changed with the colder proof. In our shared kitchen the shelf nearest the window is several degrees cooler, so I mark the container and leave it there overnight. If your loaf collapses, try shortening the warm rest before the oven rather than reducing the autolyse.

long.title: Sourdough crumb after an overnight proof in a very small shared kitchen
long.body: I mixed two loaves from the same flour and split them after the first fold. One proofed in the fridge overnight; the other stayed on the coolest shelf in the kitchen. The refrigerated loaf opened cleanly, while the warmer loaf spread before it reached the oven. I have written down the temperatures and fold times so we can compare what changed.
